title: Transactions, proxies, and races
outcome: Predict whether a transaction starts and design one test that catches a race.
cue: The wrapper must see the call.

exercises.title: Find and fix the bug
exercises.prompt: A public method calls this.reserve(), where reserve alone has @Transactional. The team expects all reservation writes to roll back. What is missing?

exercises.title: Change one condition
exercises.prompt: A send-email call succeeds but the DB transaction later rolls back. Propose a recovery design and its limitation.

trace.title: Injected bean call
trace.detail: A transaction groups database changes so they commit or roll back together. It does not automatically group a database write with an email or an external API call.

trace.title: Follow the middle steps
trace.detail:
Controller → proxy → begin → service → SQL → commit → return. If an unchecked exception leaves the service, the wrapper rolls back instead.

For a race, draw A reads 1, B reads 1, A writes 0, B writes 0. Both callers may believe they won. A transaction annotation alone does not prevent this lost update. Conditional updates or optimistic version checks turn the second attempt into a visible conflict.

trace.title: Check the result
trace.detail: A unit test using new CompleteTask(...) bypasses the proxy. It can test business decisions but cannot prove transaction interception. A transaction-wrapped test can also hide a missing production boundary.

recallPrompt: Without notes: Predict whether a transaction starts and design one test that catches a race. Give a concrete failure example.
